metricCatalog.label: Opt-in public reports
metricCatalog.description: Public reports that a publisher explicitly offered for aggregate protocol review.
metricCatalog.collectionRule: Count only a report with a public reference and explicit publication or sharing permission.

metricCatalog.label: Issue-template signals
metricCatalog.description: Consent-marked adopter or contributor signals submitted through public issue or pull-request templates.
metricCatalog.collectionRule: Count only a public template submission whose author selected the consent and anonymization fields.

metricCatalog.label: Release metadata events
metricCatalog.description: Public release and package metadata events that are useful as chronology, never as a user count.
metricCatalog.collectionRule: Record a version, date, and local verification reference only when the release is public and reproducible.

metricCatalog.label: Manually reproducible repository runs
metricCatalog.description: Pinned local replays of public or explicitly authorized repositories, reported as technical evidence rather than adoption.
metricCatalog.collectionRule: Count a run only when its revision, command, aggregate output, limitations, and local replay path are recorded.

metricCatalog.label: Repeat consented runs
metricCatalog.description: A second or later run by the same participant, retained only as an anonymized consented summary.
metricCatalog.collectionRule: Count only a separately consented summary that documents the repeat workflow without identifying the participant.

metricCatalog.label: Consented feedback records
metricCatalog.description: Anonymized feedback records that identify a confirmed, unresolved, or rejected review signal without retaining the original message.
metricCatalog.collectionRule: Count only an anonymized summary with explicit consent, a public or digest-only evidence reference, and a backlog decision.

limitations: No external public report is retained in this snapshot.
The protocol is ready for opt-in evidence but does not infer adoption from its absence.
No consented external issue-template signal is present.
Public issue volume and views are deliberately excluded as adoption proxies.
No public release series exists in this snapshot.
A local package rehearsal is not a release-stability or adoption observation.
Five pinned records are a compatibility sample with three successful and two bounded runs, not adoption or representative accuracy.
The records contain aggregate counts and digests only; no source, credentials, or participant identity is retained.
No consented repeat-run summary is retained.
A rerun performed by a maintainer does not establish participant retention.
The current feedback snapshot contains a synthetic maintainer baseline and zero external records.
No traction, retention, or reviewer-usefulness claim is made.

biases.description: Only public or explicitly authorized material can enter the protocol.
biases.effect: Private, unsuccessful, or non-public use may be systematically absent.
biases.mitigation: Publish the inclusion rule and report the eligible denominator rather than extrapolating to a population.

biases.description: A retained report is more likely to represent a completed or reviewable workflow.
biases.effect: Abandoned pilots and failed first runs can be underrepresented.
biases.mitigation: Retain bounded failures and explicit non-observed states when they are voluntarily published.

biases.description: Adopters choose whether to submit a report or consented summary.
biases.effect: Satisfied, highly engaged, or unusually blocked participants may be overrepresented.
biases.mitigation: Separate descriptive signals from adoption claims and publish the recruitment path and missingness.

biases.description: A manually replayed repository and CARTOGRAPH revision can change after a report is written.
biases.effect: Later readers may mistake a historical result for current behavior.
biases.mitigation: Pin revisions, commands, tool versions, artifact digests, and snapshot windows.

biases.description: Small cohorts can make a single report identifiable or unstable.
biases.effect: Counts can reveal a participant or encourage overinterpretation.
biases.mitigation: Suppress or defer cells below the minimum anonymization size and keep individual records out of the repository.

exclusions: Downloads, stars, views, issue volume, and CI executions are not adoption measures.
Private source, credentials, raw conversations, and unconsented repository runs are excluded.
A successful compatibility run is not converted into a user, accuracy, certification, or support count.
No metric is estimated from missing data, nonresponse, or hidden product activity.
sampling.reviewCadence: Review the protocol at each public release or before adding a new source kind; record a new snapshot and decision when semantics change.
sampling.minimumEvidence: A publishable adoption claim would require multiple independently consented, reproducible observations across the declared source kinds plus a documented limitations review.

retention.withdrawalRule: A publisher may withdraw consent before the next snapshot; the maintainer removes the summary and regenerates dependent aggregate counts and digests.

anonymization.review: A maintainer checks every proposed summary for names, contact details, private URLs, source excerpts, credentials, and combinations that could identify a small participant cohort.

deletion.requestRoute: Use the public feedback process for ordinary withdrawal requests and the private SECURITY.md route when a request contains sensitive material; do not place the material in an issue.

responsibilities.action: Delete or withdraw the original report, conversation, or authorized checkout from the publisher-controlled location and notify the maintainer before the next snapshot.
responsibilities.verification: Confirm the publisher-controlled source is no longer available and provide only a digest or public reference for the withdrawal record.

responsibilities.action: Remove the withdrawn summary, regenerate aggregate observations and provenance digests, and preserve no raw source or message copy.
responsibilities.verification: Run the offline validator and inspect the diff to confirm that the withdrawn record and dependent counts are absent.

responsibilities.action: Do not copy withdrawn summaries into a future release; document any immutable public release reference that cannot be rewritten and exclude it from current aggregates.
responsibilities.verification: Check the next release manifest and adoption snapshot for the withdrawn identifier and updated aggregate digest.

deletion.verification: Deletion is complete only when raw material is absent from the repository and the next versioned snapshot no longer counts the withdrawn signal.
exceptions: Immutable public release metadata may remain publicly addressable, but it is not reused in a current aggregate after withdrawal.
Security or legal records follow their applicable private reporting and retention route and are never copied into this protocol.

decision.rationale: The protocol is implemented and the existing five-run technical sample is reproducible, but no consented external retention, repeat-use, or adopter series is available to support a traction claim.
requiredBeforeChange: At least one new versioned snapshot with independently consented public or digest-only records.
A bias and missingness review that keeps bounded failures visible and does not turn technical runs into user counts.
A deletion rehearsal proving that a withdrawn summary disappears from future aggregates and dependent digests.
A maintainer review that preserves the no-network, no-source-upload, and no-hidden-telemetry defaults.

provenance.source: CARTOGRAPH repository-authored telemetry-free adoption measurement protocol fixture
provenance.reference: M-014 telemetry-free adoption measurement; M-004 community feedback; R-017 repository adoption evaluation; no external source retained
provenance.transformation: The protocol defines opt-in public evidence sources, aggregate metrics, sampling limitations, retention, anonymization, deletion responsibilities, and a deferred claim boundary; it retains no source bodies, private messages, credentials, or hidden telemetry.
